entries.justification: Printed: Plant tag, cost 12, 'It must be -12 C or colder to play. Gain 1 plant.', effect 'When anyone places an ocean tile, gain 2 plants.' entries.name: Decomposers
entries.justification: Printed Decomposers is an ongoing effect: 'when you play an animal, plant, or microbe tag, INCLUDING THIS, add a microbe to this card.' An ongoing effect only sees plays that happen while it is in play, and the 'including this' clause is precisely the card explicitly extending the trigger to its own arrival — and to nothing earlier. `bespokePlay` instead grants 2 extra microbes when Decomposers is played during `Phase.PRELUDES` immediately after Ecology Experts, retroactively crediting Ecology Experts' plant and microbe tags, which were played before Decomposers existed in the tableau.
entries.printedText: Decomposers (131, cost 5, microbe tag, active, requires 3% oxygen, microbe resource, 1 VP per 3 microbes): 'Effect: When you play an animal, plant, or microbe tag, including this, add a microbe to this card. 1 VP per 3 microbes on this card.'
entries.downstreamImpact: Milestone 3 (heuristic evaluation) is where it first bites, and it bites through scoring. Decomposers' VP is `resourcesHere / 3`, so 2 unearned microbes are worth up to 1 VP outright and permanently raise the card's realised value in exactly the Ecology-Experts-enabled line that makes Decomposers playable at 0% oxygen at all. M3 fits evaluation weights to observed outcomes from the M2 harness, so the weight learned for Decomposers (and for the Ecology Experts prelude that enables it) is fitted against a card that scores more than the printed card does. It also silently reaches M2's FR-DATA-1 BGA reconciliation, since BGA's implementation of the same combo is the comparison baseline. Isolation: add an Ecology-Experts-then-Decomposers game to the M2 regression seed set so the microbe count is pinned and any upstream change to the rule is detected rather than absorbed.
entries.notes: Trace confirming the magnitude, from the Engine's own control flow rather than from the spec: `Player.playCard` calls `card.play()` BEFORE pushing to `playedCards` (Player.ts:866 vs 884, with a standing comment at 852-865 acknowledging this is the wrong order), so `bespokePlay` adds 2, then the push happens, then `onCardPlayed(Decomposers)` iterates `playedCards` — now including Decomposers — and `cardTagCount` adds 1 more for its own microbe tag. Total 3, which is what tests/cards/base/Decomposers.spec.ts asserts. Printed total is 1. WHY I LANDED ON DIVERGENCE RATHER THAN R1's `undecided` FOR ECOLOGICAL ZONE, since W must adjudicate them together: the question is not what Decomposers' text means but whether an ongoing 'when you play' effect can see a play that preceded it, and the printed sequence is not ambiguous — you place Ecology Experts in your play area and gain its tags, and only then does its text instruct you to play a card, so Decomposers demonstrably arrives second. The counter-reading, which is presumably the authors' motive, is that a prelude and the card it plays form one simultaneous play so that play order should not matter; the hack exists only to make the EcoExperts-then-Decomposers order match the Decomposers-then-EcoExperts order, which the ordinary `onCardPlayed` path already handles correctly. I do not think 'order should not matter' survives contact with a card that says 'when you play'. If W prefers the simultaneity reading it must apply it to Ecological Zone too, and vice versa — the two must not land on different verdicts. Frequency note for severity: the combo is narrow (Decomposers requires 3% oxygen, unreachable during preludes except via Ecology Experts' requirement bypass) but it is exactly the line a strong agent looks for. Unrelated minor point, inert in scope: `onNonCardTagAdded` handles only Tag.PLANT, not ANIMAL or MICROBE (Decomposers.ts:43-47); no in-scope card produces a non-card animal or microbe tag, so it cannot fire wrongly today.

entries.name: Ecological Zone
entries.justification: Everything about the card is right - cost 12, Animal+Plant tags, 'requires that YOU have a greenery' correctly compiled as an own-greenery requirement (GreeneriesRequirement scopes to the player unless `all`), placement filtered to land spaces adjacent to ANY greenery, 1 VP per 2 animals, and 2 animals when played normally (its own animal and plant tags via onCardPlayed after the card enters playedCards). The one open question is bespokePlay lines 66-70: if the card is played during Phase.PRELUDES immediately after Ecology Experts, it silently grants a THIRD animal, on the theory that the card played via Ecology Experts should retroactively see Ecology Experts' own plant tag. Nothing in the printed text supports a retroactive trigger - an effect applies only while its card is in play, and Ecology Experts was fully played (and its onCardPlayed pass already run) before Ecological Zone entered the tableau. Against that, the Engine applies the same rule consistently to Decomposers (+2 microbes for Ecology Experts' plant and microbe tags, src/server/cards/base/Decomposers.ts:48-53), which is what a genuine 'the nested card play is simultaneous with the prelude' reading would produce. I cannot settle which reading the printed rules intend, so: undecided.
entries.printedText: Ecological Zone (128), 12 M€, blue/active, Animal + Plant tags. 'Requires that you have a greenery tile.' Effect: 'When you play an animal or plant tag, including these, add an animal to this card.' 'Place this tile adjacent to ANY greenery.' 1 VP per 2 animals on this card.
entries.notes: If W resolves this against the Engine it is a scoring divergence (animals are 1 VP per 2) and should escalate under K5. Impact is small and rare: it needs Ecology Experts and Ecological Zone (or Decomposers) together in the prelude phase. Note that the Engine's condition is `phase === PRELUDES && playedCards.last() === ECOLOGY_EXPERTS`, which does not check that this card was actually played *via* Ecology Experts, and does not extend the same retroactive credit to any other previously-played card - i.e. it is a special case, not a general rule, which is itself weak evidence that it is a hack rather than a ruling. onCardPlayed and onNonCardTagAdded (plant tags added by non-card sources) both match the printed effect.

entries.name: Flooding
entries.justification: Printed: place an ocean, then you MAY remove 4 M€ from the owner of one tile adjacent to that ocean. The implementation defers PlaceOceanTile, then collects adjacent spaces that have both an owner and a tile, offers a SelectPlayer plus an explicit decline option, and calls target.attack(..., MEGACREDITS, 4) WITHOUT `stealing`, i.e. the 4 M€ is destroyed rather than gained - which is what the printed card says. Two things that could have gone wrong do not: `Game.simpleAddTile` sets `space.player = undefined` for OCEAN tiles (Game.ts:1449-1458), so an adjacent ocean correctly has no owner; and the `space.tile` test correctly excludes a Land-Claim-marked but empty space.
entries.printedText: Flooding (188). 7 M€, event, no tags, -1 VP. 'Place an ocean tile. If there are tiles adjacent to this ocean tile, you may remove 4 M€ from the owner of one of those tiles.'
entries.notes: Printed says 'remove 4 M€', not 'up to 4' - so the fixed amount is correct, and Stock.add's clamp (Stock.ts:24) handles a target holding fewer than 4 without going negative. This is the exact contrast case for the 'up to' finding on Sabotage/Hired Raiders below. Two inert restrictions: the implementation excludes the placing player's own adjacent tiles (self-removal is a strictly pointless 'may', and Mons Insurance, the only card that could make it non-pointless, is promo/out of scope), and if all 9 oceans are already placed PlaceOceanTile never invokes the andThen, so no removal happens - which is right, since no ocean means no adjacency.

entries.name: Immigrant City
entries.justification: The printed card's production box (-1 energy, -2 M€ production) is paid when the card is played, before the city tile is placed and therefore before the card's own 'when a city tile is placed, including this' trigger can pay any of it back; M€ production floors at -5, so the printed card is unplayable at M€ production -4 or -5. The Engine instead defers both production losses until after placement (bespokePlay lines 57-64), so the +1 trigger resolves first (Priority.GAIN_RESOURCE_OR_PRODUCTION 47 before Priority.LOSE_RESOURCE_OR_PRODUCTION 48), and bespokeCanPlay accordingly permits play at M€ production >= -4, or at ANY M€ production when the player holds Tharsis Republic. Both extra states are deliberate and asserted in tests/cards/base/ImmigrantCity.spec.ts ('Can play at -4 M€ production', 'Tharsis can play at -5 M€ production'), so this is a considered Engine interpretation rather than an oversight - but it is more permissive than the printed card in a way that changes which moves are legal.
entries.printedText: Immigrant City (200), 13 M€, blue/active, City + Building tags. Effect: 'When a city tile is placed, including this, increase your M€ production 1 step.' Production box: -1 energy, -2 M€. 'Decrease your energy production 1 step and decrease your M€ production 2 steps. Place a city tile.'
entries.downstreamImpact: Bites first at M2 (baselines and the FR-DATA-1 BGA reconciliation are computed on a game whose legal move set differs from the printed game in this state) and retroactively at M1: the AC-1 legality run measured legality against the Engine's own canPlay, so an Engine-side over-permission is invisible to it by construction. It also bites M3/M4: the enumerator will offer Immigrant City in states where the printed game forbids it, so any evaluation weight or search line that leans on 'Immigrant City is always available once you have a city space' is fitted to a slightly different game. Concrete repro: 2p Tharsis, player has energy production 1, M€ production -4 (reachable via repeated Hackers-class attacks), an available non-city-adjacent land space, and 13 M€. Expected (printed): the card cannot be played, because the -2 M€ production step cannot be taken from -4. Actual (Engine): canPlay is true; the card is played; the placed city triggers +1 (to -3), then -2 applies (to -5), ending at energy production 0 and M€ production -5. With Tharsis Republic in the tableau the same happens from M€ production -5, ending unchanged at -5, i.e. the printed card's entire M€ production cost is skipped. Recommend an upstream report; do not patch src/.
entries.notes: The verdict rests on one interpretive premise: that a card's effects resolve in printed order (production box on play, tile placement after) and that a decrease of your own production is a cost that must be fully payable at that moment. If W disagrees with that premise the finding collapses to `undecided`. The Tharsis Republic branch is the stronger half of the case - at M€ production -5 there is no ordering at all under which 'decrease your M€ production 2 steps' is performable, yet the Engine allows it and asserts a net-zero M€ production change. Reachability is low: M€ production <= -4 requires sustained attacks, and Immigrant City was played 173 times in the 1,500-game sweep with no record of the M€ production at play time.

entries.justification: Printed: 8 M€, Building tag, 1 VP, 'When any city tile is placed, gain 2 M€' -- explicitly ANY player's city, not just the owner's. The Engine's hook signature is onTilePlaced(cardOwner, activePlayer, space), dispatched from Game.triggerForAllCards which walks every player's tableau (Game.ts:1401, 1410-1416); the card gains to `cardOwner` and uses `activePlayer` only to pick Priority.OPPONENT_TRIGGER for deferred ordering. entries.printedText: Rover Construction (#038, 8 M€, Building tag, blue/Active, 1 VP). Effect: When any city tile is placed, gain 2 M€.
entries.notes: Metadata verified: cost 8, tags [building], ACTIVE, no requirements, victoryPoints 1. Trigger set checked in both directions. Over-firing: isCitySpace tests CITY_TILES = {CITY, CAPITAL, OCEAN_CITY, RED_CITY, NEW_HOLLAND} (common/TileType.ts:119) evaluated after the tile is placed, so only genuine city tiles fire, and each addTile dispatches the hook exactly once. Under-firing: every in-scope city placement routes through Game.addTile (Game.addCity -> addTile), including the reserved-area cities Ganymede Colony and Phobos Space Haven, which per the standard ruling do count as city tiles placed. The unused BoardType parameter means a Moon call would also be considered, but Moon tile types are not in CITY_TILES, and the Moon is out of Nadia's scope anyway.

entries.justification: Printed: requires oxygen 6% or less; action 'spend 1 M€ to reveal the top card of the draw deck, if that card has a microbe tag add a science resource here'; 3 VP if there is one or more science resource here. Metadata is cost 3, science tag, resourceType SCIENCE, requirements {oxygen: 6, max}, victoryPoints 'special' with the getVictoryPoints override returning 3 iff resourceCount > 0 - a threshold, not a per-resource count, which is what the printed card says. The action pays via SelectPaymentDeferred(1) and only then draws, logs the reveal publicly, adds the resource on a microbe tag, and discards the revealed card (the printed card does not spell out the discard; the standard ruling does).

Belief-model note for M4: the reveal is logged with no `reservedFor`, i.e. it is public information, and the revealed card goes to the discard pile - both facts the card-flow belief update must consume.

entries.name: CrediCor
entries.justification: Printed: start with 57 M€, no tags, 'When you pay for a card or standard project with a basic cost of 20 M€ or more, you gain 4 M€.' Both dispatchers are own-player-only (Player.ts:921 and StandardProjectCard.ts:50-53). Timing is right in both: Player.playCard pays at line 835 before onCardPlayed at 903, and StandardProjectCard.payAndExecute pays before projectPlayed triggers the hook, so the 4 M€ can never help afford the thing that produced it.

entries.name: Helion

entries.name: Tharsis Republic
entries.justification: Printed: start with 40 M€; first action place a city tile; when any city tile is placed ON MARS increase your M€ production 1 step; when YOU place a city tile gain 3 M€. `onTilePlaced` implements both clauses with their different scopes correctly — the 3 M€ is conditioned on `cardOwner.id === activePlayer.id` and carries no on-Mars test (the printed clause has none), while the production step is conditioned on `space.spaceType !== SpaceType.COLONY` and applies to any player's placement.
entries.printedText: Tharsis Republic (R31, corporation, building tag, 40 M€): 'You start with 40 M€. As your first action in the game, place a city tile. Effect: When any city tile is placed ON MARS, increase your M€ production 1 step. Effect: When you place a city tile, gain 3 M€.'
entries.notes: The COLONY test is the load-bearing part and it is right, which is not obvious: the base game DOES have off-Mars city tiles — Ganymede Colony (081) and Phobos Space Haven both place a city on a reserved space, and `BoardBuilder.ts:90-91` builds both as `colonySpace(...)`, i.e. `SpaceType.COLONY`. So those two cities correctly pay their owner 3 M€ and correctly do NOT raise anyone's M€ production. `Board.isCitySpace` (Board.ts:279-281) keys on the CITY_TILES set, so Capital counts as a city, as printed. R1'S IMMIGRANT CITY FINDING IS NOT THIS CARD'S DEFECT. I confirmed the mechanism from this side: both of Tharsis Republic's triggers are `Priority.GAIN_RESOURCE_OR_PRODUCTION` (47) — `GainProduction.ts:16`, `GainResourcesDeferred.ts:19` — which is what lets them resolve ahead of a `LOSE_RESOURCE_OR_PRODUCTION` (48) cost queued in the same play. Deferring a trigger is the ordinary and correct thing for a trigger to do; the divergence R1 found lives in the card that lets a later trigger fund an up-front cost, not in the corporation that fires the trigger. `bespokePlay`'s +2 M€ production compensation for the two neutral solo cities is unreachable in Nadia's configuration (`Game.isSoloMode()` is `players.length === 1`, Game.ts:532; `gameFactory.ts` builds 2-4p only) and I make no claim about its solo correctness.

entries.name: Aquifer
entries.justification: Printed cost 18 and the printed effect (place an ocean tile, with its TR) are exact: cost: 18, tr: {oceans: 1}, actionEssence defers PlaceOceanTile, and addOcean grants the TR only while oceans remain. canPayWith returns {} in every Nadia game (its Kuiper Cooperative branch is out of configuration), so the project correctly takes neither steel nor titanium and takes heat only via Helion. The one unsettled point is that at 9 oceans canAct only calls addWarning('maxoceans') and then returns super.canAct, so paying 18 M€ for nothing is an enabled, server-validated legal move.
entries.printedText: Aquifer standard project (SP2): 'Spend 18 M€ to place an ocean tile.'
entries.notes: THE SHARED OPEN QUESTION (one register row for all five of Aquifer, Asteroid:SP, Convert Heat, Aquifer Pumping, Water Import From Europa): may a player take an action whose entire printed effect is an increase to an already-maxed global parameter? The Engine's answer is yes-with-a-warning, applied consistently and stated in as many words at ArtificialLake.ts:35 ('Card is playable, it just has no effect'). It is defensible under the rulebook's 'increases beyond the goal are ignored and give no TR', and the Engine is scrupulous about the TR half (Game.increaseTemperature:1283, increaseOxygenLevel:1187 and addOcean:1576 all return before granting TR). But it is a rules interpretation I cannot settle from the printed card text, and it is a *legality* question, not a cosmetic one: it puts a strictly-dominated, money-burning move into the enumerated legal set. Practical consequence for Nadia: the random-legal agent will occasionally take it (Aquifer alone was played 11,415 times in the 1,500-game sweep), so AC-1-style random baselines burn some M€ this way; any evaluating agent will never choose it, so M3+ is unaffected. If the printed rules do forbid no-effect actions, this is an over-permissive legal set rather than a wrong effect — no state the Engine reaches is mis-scored either way.

Cost 25 is transcribed correctly, `actionEssence` defers `PlaceCityTile` and adds exactly 1 M€ production, and `canAct` correctly refuses when the board offers no legal city space before falling through to the affordability check in `StandardProjectCard.canAct`.
entries.printedText: City (SP4, standard project): 'Spend 25 M€ to place a city tile and increase your M€ production 1 step.'
entries.notes: `canPayWith` is inert under Nadia's options: it returns `{steel: true}` only when the player holds Prefabrication of Human Habitats, which is a Pathfinders card and not in any in-scope manifest, so the card is always M€-only here — correct per the printed rules, which allow steel only for building-tagged projects. Phase I classes this `uncovered` / `instantiated-but-inert`: it has no dedicated spec and `actionEssence` executed zero times in the whole Engine suite, so the 10,187 plays across the 1,500-game sweep are the ONLY execution evidence this card has. That is a question-4 gap on a card the agent uses in essentially every game, and it deserves a register row on those grounds even though the correctness read is clean — but it is not a correctness finding and I have not treated it as one.

entries.name: Sell Patents
entries.justification: Printed standard project: discard any number of cards, gain 1 M€ each. `canAct` gates on a non-empty hand, `action()` offers a `SelectCard` over the whole hand with `max = hand size` (and `SelectCard`'s default `min` of 1, SelectCard.ts:38, so a zero-card no-op sale is not offered), credits `cards.length` M€ and discards them. `actionEssence` is a deliberate no-op because this card never routes through `payAndExecute`. The two exclusions are printed, not invented: Standard Technology's own text exempts selling patents, and `projectPlayed` keeps it out of `standardProjectsThisGeneration`.
entries.printedText: Sell Patents (SP8, standard project, cost 0): 'Discard any number of cards to gain that amount of M€' (1 M€ per card discarded).
entries.notes: 0 PLAYS IN THE SWEEP IS AN INSTRUMENT BLIND SPOT, NOT A DEFECT SIGNAL — checked, not assumed. The card is genuinely reachable: `Game.getStandardProjects()` filters it out of the standard-project list (Game.ts:1637) exactly as the census records, and `Player.getActions()` instead constructs a throwaway `SellPatentsStandardProject`, tests `canAct`, and pushes `sellPatents.action(this)` directly into the turn's top-level `OrOptions` (Player.ts:1660-1664). That path calls `action()`, whose continuation calls `projectPlayed` itself — it NEVER calls `payAndExecute`, and `payAndExecute` is precisely the chokepoint phase M's sweep wraps for standard projects (playSweep.ts:122-127). So Sell Patents is structurally invisible to the sweep and its count would read 0 no matter how often the agent used it. This is a K4 finding for W, not a K5 one: the K4 denominator's `reachable-by-other-route` row cannot be discharged by this artifact, and the honest statement is 'not observable by this instrument', not 'never played'. Corroborating evidence that the card is exercised at all: phase I records it `behavioural` with executionCount 25 in the Engine suite. If W wants the real number, the fix is a third chokepoint on `SellPatentsStandardProject.prototype.action` — but that is phase M's file, and this batch changed nothing.

The action places the greenery (raising oxygen and TR) and then deducts the plants.

The addGreenery-then-deduct ordering is safe: a greenery placed on a plant-bonus space credits the bonus first and the fixed deduction still lands correctly. cost marked false because StandardActionCard takes no cost property (the census's 0 is a default, not a printed cost); the printed price is plants, and it was checked. entries.name: Energy Tapping
entries.justification: Printed: 'Decrease any energy production 1 step and increase your own 1 step.' Two effects joined by 'and', resolved in written order, and TM's general rule is that a part of an effect that cannot be carried out is ignored - so when NO player has energy production the decrease is ignored and the player still gains 1 step. The implementation detects exactly that case and inverts the order: it defers GainProduction FIRST, then DecreaseAnyProduction, which now finds the player themselves as the only legal target and forces them to take the step back (the comment says so explicitly: 'This Player must gain their energy production in order to lose it'). Net effect in the engine is zero production for 3 M€ and -1 VP, where the printed card gives +1 energy production. When somebody does have energy production the implementation matches the printed card exactly, including 'any' correctly including the player themselves.
entries.printedText: Energy Tapping (201). 3 M€, power tag, automated, -1 VP. 'Decrease any energy production 1 step and increase your own 1 step.'
entries.downstreamImpact: Reproduction: 2p game, generation 1, neither player has built energy production (both at 0, no Thorgate, no energy-production prelude). Player A plays Energy Tapping for 3 M€. EXPECTED (printed): the '-1 energy production (any player)' has no legal target and is ignored; A's energy production goes 0 -> 1; A takes -1 VP. ACTUAL (engine): GainProduction runs first, A goes 0 -> 1; DecreaseAnyProduction then finds A as the sole target, presents a one-option SelectPlayer, and A must remove their own step, ending at 0. A paid 3 M€ and 1 VP for nothing, and answered a decision that should not exist. The engine's own spec (tests/cards/base/EnergyTapping.spec.ts, 'play - no targets') asserts this net-zero outcome, so it is intentional rather than accidental. First bites at Milestone 2: FR-DATA-1's required BGA<->engine reconciliation compares per-card win rates, and Energy Tapping (and Power Supply Consortium, see notes) is materially weaker in this engine than in the printed game, so its expert-dataset row is not comparable. It bites again at Milestone 3, where any hand-written evaluation term that scores Energy Tapping as '+1 energy production' will be wrong in exactly the early-generation states where the card is most often affordable and most often played. Recommend reporting upstream (H10: record, do not patch src/).
entries.notes: Scope of the pattern: the identical gain-first special case appears verbatim in PowerSupplyConsortium.ts:34-44, GreatEscarpmentConsortium and AsteroidMiningConsortium. The latter two are protected by their own printed requirements ('requires that you have steel/titanium production'), so their zero-target branch is unreachable; only Energy Tapping and Power Supply Consortium (whose requirement is 2 power tags, which does not imply energy production) can actually reach it. Power Supply Consortium is outside my batch - flagging it so the write-up can treat the pair together. Residual uncertainty, stated honestly: my anchor is the general TM rule ('do as much as you can; ignore what you cannot') plus the card's written order, not a card-specific FAQ entry I can quote verbatim. If the write-up phase judges that anchor insufficient this should become `undecided` rather than `matches` - it should not be recorded as agreement. I set escalates=true even though the divergence is in production rather than literally legality or scoring, because production is the card's entire effect and it propagates to resources and VP; the extra forced SelectPlayer decision is also a spurious node in M4's search tree.

entries.name: Great Escarpment Consortium
entries.justification: Printed: requires that you have steel production; decrease any steel production 1 step and increase your own 1 step. The requirement is transcribed as `{production: Resource.STEEL, count: 1}`, and both halves are deferred with the decrease resolving first — `DecreaseAnyProduction` is `Priority.ATTACK_OPPONENT` (44) and `GainProduction` is `GAIN_RESOURCE_OR_PRODUCTION` (47), so written order is preserved regardless of the order they were queued in.
entries.printedText: Great Escarpment Consortium (061, cost 6, no tags, automated, no VP): 'Requires that you have steel production. Decrease any steel production 1 step and increase your own 1 step.'
entries.notes: This card is the control that makes the Power Supply Consortium finding legible: because the printed requirement guarantees the acting player has ≥1 steel production, an eligible target always exists and the Engine never needs — and never applies — the gain-first workaround. If the two cards were treated as a pair the divergence in the other one would be invisible. Cosmetic only, recorded and dismissed: the renderer calls `pb.minus().steel(-1, {all})`, a double negation where every sibling card writes `steel(1)`; it affects the card image only, not the behaviour.

entries.name: Hackers
entries.justification: Printed effect and every metadata field transcribe exactly (cost 3, no tags, -1 VP, -1 energy production / -2 any M€ production / +2 own M€ production). The open point is resolution order: the card's own +2 M€ production is applied immediately by the declarative `behavior` block, while the printed-first '-2 any M€ production' is deferred (`DecreaseAnyProduction`, Priority.ATTACK_OPPONENT=44) and therefore evaluates its target list against the post-gain state. `canHaveProductionReduced` (Player.ts:400-403) treats M€ production as reducible only down to -5, so a player at M€ production -5 or -4 is not an eligible target before the gain but is after it. Whether the printed card licenses that depends on whether a production box resolves in written order or nets simultaneously, which I cannot settle from the card face.
entries.printedText: Hackers (125, cost 3, no tags, automated, -1 VP): 'Decrease your Energy production 1 step and any M€ production 2 steps. Increase your M€ production 2 steps.'
entries.notes: Concrete state that separates the readings: 2p, acting player M€ production -5, opponent M€ production -5, acting player has ≥1 energy production. Engine: +2 M€ production (→ -3), then the attack finds exactly one eligible target (the acting player, reducible 2) and `SelectPlayer` forces it → back to -5; net effect of the card is -1 energy production, -1 VP, no M€ production. Printed-order reading: no player can absorb -2 at the moment the decrease is written, so the decrease is simply not performed and the player ends at -3. Same family as this batch's Power Supply Consortium finding and R1's Immigrant City finding — W should adjudicate the three together rather than card-by-card, since the Engine is internally consistent about it. Separately (question 4, not question 3): phase I classes Hackers `uncovered` / `instantiated-but-inert` — tests/cards/base/Hackers.spec.ts only calls `canPlay()`, so `bespokePlay`, i.e. the entire M€-stealing half of the card, is never executed anywhere in the Engine suite. 233 plays in the sweep are the only execution evidence.

entries.name: Hired Raiders
entries.justification: Printed: 'Steal UP TO 2 steel, or 3 M€ from any player.' The implementation offers, per opponent, only the maximum: steal 2 steel (if they have any) or steal 3 M€ (if they have any), plus a global 'Do not steal'. The printed 'up to' grants a free choice of any amount from 0 to N; the engine's legal set is therefore {max, 0} instead of {0..N}. Everything else is right: it uses attack(..., {stealing: true}) so the thief GAINS the resources (Stock.steal clamps to what the target actually has, Stock.ts:64-72), no option is offered against a target holding none, and the amounts 2/3 and cost 1 are correct.
entries.printedText: Hired Raiders (124). 1 M€, event, no tags. 'Steal up to 2 steel, or 3 M€ from any player.'
entries.notes: escalates is deliberately false: this is a universal engine convention for every 'remove/steal up to N' card (Asteroid, Sabotage, Deimos Down, ...), not a card-specific error, and the omitted intermediate amounts are dominated in almost every position - taking more from an opponent never costs the thief anything directly. The one non-contrived exception is award denial in 3-4p: the Miner award counts steel+titanium RESOURCES, so removing more from opponent B can hand Miner to opponent C. The write-up should adjudicate this once for the whole class rather than per card. Also note the self-target case ('any player' includes yourself) is excluded, which is inert. The solo branch (lines 33-44) adds resources with no source player and is unreachable in Nadia's 2-4p config.

entries.name: Indentured Workers
entries.justification: Printed: Event, 0 M€, no tags, -1 VP, 'The next card you play this generation costs 8 M€ less.' The override returns 8 exactly while player.lastCardPlayed === INDENTURED_WORKERS, and all three printed dimensions check out: magnitude is 8; scope is project-card plays only (getCardDiscount is consulted solely from Player.getCardCost(card: IProjectCard) at Player.ts:708-721 -- standard projects use the separate getStandardProjectDiscount path, and research-phase card buying uses cardCost, so neither is discounted, matching 'the next card you play'); and it is consumed exactly once, because Player.checkPaymentAndPlayCard computes getCardCost (line 750) before playCard overwrites lastCardPlayed with the card just played (line 848), after which the override returns 0. Generation expiry is honoured because Player.pass() clears lastCardPlayed (Player.ts:1141) and pass() is the only route by which an in-scope player ends a generation, so an unused discount cannot leak into the next generation.
entries.printedText: Indentured Workers (#195, 0 M€, no tags, red/Event, -1 VP). The next card you play this generation costs 8 M€ less.
entries.notes: Checked as a legality question, not only an economy one. The discount enters affordability through Player.affordOptionsForCard -> getCardCost -> canPlay (Player.ts:1239-1255), so it correctly widens the legal move set for exactly one card and no more, and Math.max(cost, 0) at Player.ts:728 prevents a negative cost. Owner scope is correct: getCardCost only walks the paying player's own tableau. The card stays in the tableau permanently (events remain in PlayedCards.array, so the iterator still reaches them -- worth stating because the existing spec calls card.getCardDiscount directly and would not have caught an events-excluded-from-tableau bug). One residual, non-divergent observation for later phases: the expiry is implemented as 'lastCardPlayed changed or the player passed' rather than an explicit generation stamp; that is equivalent under Nadia's configuration only because every player passes to end a generation and no in-scope card sets lastCardPlayed outside Player.playCard. Out-of-scope modules (e.g. prelude2 RedAppeasement's forced pass, promo Double Down) touch the same flag, so a later expansion-scope change should re-check this.

entries.justification: Printed: Science/Earth/Building tags, cost 10, holds science resources, 1 VP, 'When you play a science tag, including this, either add a science resource to this card, or remove a science resource from this card to draw a card.' Implementation matches every metadata field, and onCardPlayed defers one choice per science tag on the card just played (Tags.cardTagCount counts literal tags on that one card), evaluating resourceCount at execution time so the add/remove choice is correct for each of several triggers on the same card. 'Including this' works because Player.playCard pushes the card into playedCards (Player.ts:884) before calling onCardPlayed (Player.ts:903), and the loop at Player.ts:921 is over the acting player's own tableau only — correctly not other players' plays.

(1) When resourceCount is 0 the card silently auto-adds instead of presenting a one-option choice — correct, since 'remove' is illegal, but it means the Agent sees no decision point there. (2) The Engine fixes the resolution order of a player's own simultaneous triggers via the Priority enum (Priority.OLYMPUS_CONFERENCE deliberately ordered ahead of SPONSORED_ACADEMIES/DISCARD_AND_DRAW, src/server/deferredActions/Priority.ts:22-40); the printed rules let the player choose. Here the fixed order (Olympus Conference before Mars University) weakly dominates for the player, so no reachable loss. onNonCardTagAdded(SCIENCE) is only reachable via Colony trade (Colony.ts:108) and Underworld (UnderworldExpansion.ts:417) — both out of Nadia's configuration, so that branch is dead code here, not a divergence.

entries.name: Power Supply Consortium
entries.justification: Printed: 'Requires 2 power tags. Decrease any Energy production 1 step and increase your own 1 step.' When NO player has any energy production there is no legal target for the decrease, so under the standard rule for an effect that cannot be carried out it is simply not performed and the player still gains 1 energy production. The Engine instead detects that case and inverts the order specifically to manufacture a target — it grants the +1 first, which makes the acting player the sole eligible target, and `DecreaseAnyProduction` then forces the self-decrease because `targets[0] === this.player`. The card becomes a complete no-op instead of a +1.
entries.printedText: Power Supply Consortium (160, cost 5, power tag, automated, no VP): 'Requires 2 power tags. Decrease any Energy production 1 step and increase your own 1 step.'
entries.downstreamImpact: Milestone 3 (heuristic evaluation) first, then Milestone 4. The divergence is a full step of energy production — a permanent, compounding resource — on a 5 M€ card, so the card's true value in the no-target state is 'pay 5 M€ for a power tag and nothing else' where the printed card is 'pay 5 M€ for a power tag and +1 energy production'. M3 fits card weights to harness outcomes, so it will learn a systematically depressed weight for Power Supply Consortium and, worse, will learn it from a state (nobody has energy production) that is most common in the EARLY game, which is exactly when the card is most likely to be played. M4's search inherits the same evaluation. Isolation: pin the no-target case in the M2 regression seed set with the expected end-state energy production asserted, so the value is fixed by data rather than inferred, and flag the card in the M3 feature schema as rules-contested until upstream rules on it. This is ONE defect in TWO cards, not two defects: the block is duplicated verbatim from Energy Tapping (R3's finding), the two are the only in-scope cards that reach it, and they compound — so it should take a single register row and a single upstream report covering both.
entries.notes: ANSWERS R3's QUESTION ON THE ENERGY TAPPING PAIR: NO, the printed requirement does NOT make the zero-target branch unreachable. `PowerSupplyConsortium.ts:35-45` is byte-for-byte identical to `EnergyTapping.ts:35-45`, comment included, and the requirement that separates them is a TAG requirement (2 power tags), not a production requirement. Concrete generation-1 line, all in-scope base/corpera cards, no attack and no expansion needed: Power Infrastructure (base, 4 M€, `tags: [Tag.POWER, Tag.BUILDING]`, PowerInfrastructure.ts:17-18 — it has NO `behavior` production block at all, its effect is the spend-energy-for-M€ action) gives a power tag and zero energy production; Energy Tapping (3 M€, power tag) gives the second power tag and, if nobody yet has energy production, lands in its OWN zero-target branch and leaves the player at zero; the player now satisfies '2 power tags' with 0 energy production and, with all opponents also at 0, playing Power Supply Consortium reaches the branch. Printed outcome of that line is +2 energy production; Engine outcome is 0, plus the -1 VP Energy Tapping charges. THE TWO DEFECTS COMPOUND — Energy Tapping is one of the very cards that manufactures the precondition for Power Supply Consortium's copy of the bug. Energy Saving (15 M€, power tag, `production: {energy: {cities: {}}}`) is a third power tag that yields zero energy production while no city is on the board. I ALSO AGREE WITH R3's ANCHOR, and reached this verdict independently before R3's finding arrived: the general 'perform as much as you can, skip what you cannot' rule plus written resolution order. I have no card-specific FAQ line to quote either, and I record that as the weakest link in both entries — but the Engine's own conduct is corroborating, because it does not merely fail to skip the unperformable part, it actively reorders the card to create a target that the printed sequence never has. Contrast Great Escarpment Consortium, the sibling in this batch, which requires you to HAVE steel production and therefore always has a target; R3's reading that the printed requirement is what makes the steel/titanium consortium cards safe is correct, and that asymmetry is presumably why only the two energy cards needed the workaround. THIS IS A DELIBERATE ENGINE DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT, and any upstream report should say so: the code carries an explanatory comment ('If no player has energy production, then This Player must gain their energy production in order to lose it') and tests/cards/base/PowerSupplyConsortium.spec.ts:31-44 ('Can play - no targets') asserts the net-zero outcome explicitly. That spec is the same source as the implementation and is not independent evidence for the rule. The normal branch is correct: the decrease is deferred first and the gain chained after it, so a player who is the ONLY holder of energy production is properly forced to take it from themselves for a net zero, which the printed card does require. entries.name: Viral Enhancers
entries.justification: Printed: Science/Microbe tags, cost 9, no VP, 'When you play a plant, microbe, or an animal tag, including this, gain 1 plant or add 1 resource to THAT CARD.' Implementation counts plant/microbe/animal tags on the played card, and when that card cannot hold animal or microbe resources it grants plants directly with no illusory choice — which is exhaustive under Nadia's configuration (I enumerated every in-scope card carrying a resourceType: no base/Corporate-Era/Prelude card has a plant, microbe or animal tag together with a resourceType other than ANIMAL or MICROBE). Own-plays only, and 'including this' is satisfied: playing Viral Enhancers itself triggers once on its own microbe tag and, since Viral Enhancers holds no resources, correctly resolves as +1 plant.
entries.printedText: Viral Enhancers (074) — Cost 9. Tags: Science, Microbe. Effect: When you play a plant, microbe, or an animal tag, including this, gain 1 plant or add 1 resource to THAT CARD.
entries.notes: TWO THINGS FOR W. (a) R1's Moss/Nitrophilic Moss transient negative-plants observation is CONFIRMED, and the defect is not in Viral Enhancers. Moss.ts:33-42 and NitrophilicMoss.ts:34-42 accept the play when `player.plants` is short but Viral Enhancers is in the tableau, then bespokePlay does the raw `player.plants--` / `player.plants -= 2` (Player.ts:225-227 assigns straight through to stock, bypassing Stock.add's clamp at src/server/player/Stock.ts:24-41), and only afterwards does Player.playCard reach onCardPlayed (Player.ts:903) where Viral Enhancers grants the plant back. Net result is 0, but the intermediate state is stock.plants = -1 (or -1/0 for Nitrophilic Moss) and no logIllegalState is emitted because the raw setter is used. This is the Immigrant-City pattern (a gain arriving later in the play is counted toward an up-front cost) and it lives on the Moss cards' bespokeCanPlay/bespokePlay, not on Viral Enhancers, whose own +1 plant is exactly what the printed card promises. It matters to the Agent because a snapshot taken mid-play would carry a negative resource. (b) NESTED-PLAY ASYMMETRY. EcologicalZone.ts:73-76 carries an explicit hack granting one extra animal when it is played during Phase.PRELUDES immediately after Ecology Experts, i.e. crediting Ecology Experts' own already-played plant tag to a card that entered play afterwards. Viral Enhancers has no such hack, and Ecology Experts carries BOTH a plant and a microbe tag — exactly the tags Viral Enhancers responds to. So if W rules the Ecological Zone hack correct, Viral Enhancers under-fires by 2 triggers when played through Ecology Experts; if W rules it incorrect, Ecological Zone over-fires by 1. The Engine cannot be right about both. My reading of the printed rules is that an ongoing effect applies only from the moment its card is in play, which makes Viral Enhancers correct and Ecological Zone the outlier — but W must adjudicate the two together. Olympus Conference, Mars University, Media Group and Point Luna are unaffected: Ecology Experts and Eccentric Sponsor (the only two in-scope cards that defer a PlayProjectCard) carry no science, Earth or event tag between them.

entries.name: Virus

ranking.marker: src/server/cards/base/Virus.ts:36 - TODO "Special case for Mons Insurance owner"

entries.justification: Printed Virus lets you remove up to 2 animals OR 5 plants from ANY player, which under the red-border/'any' rule includes yourself. The animal half honours that (`RemoveResourcesFromCard` with the default source 'all' includes the acting player's own animal cards). The plant half does not: `bespokePlay` takes `RemoveAnyPlants`' option list and does `options.slice(0, -1)` on the assumption that the last entry is the skip option, but `RemoveAnyPlants.execute()` pushes 'Skip removing plants' and THEN appends the acting player's own-plants option when they hold plants. So when the Virus player has plants, `slice(0, -1)` discards their own-plants option and keeps the skip option, which Virus then duplicates with its own 'Skip removal'.
entries.printedText: Virus (050, cost 1, microbe tag, event, no VP): 'Remove up to 2 Animals or 5 Plants from any player.'
entries.notes: MARKER `Virus.ts:36` ('Special case for Mons Insurance owner') VERIFIED INERT, on two independent grounds, neither assumed: (1) it sits inside `if (player.game.isSoloMode())` (Virus.ts:35) and `Game.isSoloMode()` is `players.length === 1` (Game.ts:532), while `gameFactory.ts` builds 2-4 player games only; (2) Mons Insurance lives in `src/server/cards/promo/` and is registered only in `PromoCardManifest.ts:206`, and `promoCardsOption` is false under Nadia's options, so `game.monsInsuranceOwner` can never be set. The same reasoning discharges the `resolveInsurance()` hook that `Production.add` fires on every stolen production step in this batch's other attack cards. Reproduction for the divergence: 2p, Virus player holds 3 plants, opponent holds 5 plants. Expected (printed): the choice set includes removing 5 plants from the opponent, removing 3 from yourself, and declining. Actual: removing from the opponent, and TWO behaviourally identical decline options; your own plants are not offered. Severity argued as low for correctness — the lost option is strictly self-harming and no rational agent selects it — but it is legality-affecting in the strict sense and I have not hidden it inside `matches`. The duplicate no-op branch is the part with a real Nadia-side cost: it inflates the branching factor of this decision by one behaviourally-identical arm, which biases uniform-random rollouts at M4 (two of N arms are the same move) and doubles this node's weight in any visit-count statistic. tests/cards/base/Virus.spec.ts:36-40 asserts the acting player's plants are untouched, so the Engine's authors locked the behaviour in — same source, not independent evidence. One point I did not settle and am not calling a divergence: the animal half removes 2 from a single selected card rather than splitting across cards; that is the Engine-wide convention for card-resource removal, not specific to Virus.

entries.justification: Printed: Space and Earth tags, start with 38 M€ and 1 titanium production, 'When you play an Earth tag, including this, draw a card.' Metadata agrees exactly, and onCardPlayed draws once per Earth tag on the played card (Tags.cardTagCount, literal tags on that card). 'Including this' is satisfied because Player.playCorporationCard pushes the corporation into playedCards (Player.ts:975) before calling onCardPlayed (Player.ts:1003), so Point Luna draws one card for its own Earth tag on selection. entries.printedText: Point Luna (R10) — Corporation, Space and Earth tags. You start with 38 M€ and 1 titanium production. Effect: When you play an Earth tag, including this, draw a card.
entries.notes: Draws synchronously inside the hook rather than deferring. WILD-TAG CHECK (cross-cutting; applies equally to Olympus Conference, Mars University and Viral Enhancers in this batch): Tags.cardTagCount (src/server/player/Tags.ts:152-165) does NOT credit Tag.WILD, so playing either of the two in-scope wild-tag cards — Research Coordination (P40, a project card, cost 4) or Research Network (P28, a prelude) — triggers none of the on-play tag hooks. I anchored this on the printed wild-tag text itself, 'After being played, when you perform an action, the wild tag counts as any tag of your choice': the flexibility begins AFTER the card has been played and is scoped to actions you subsequently perform, so the act of playing the wild-tag card is not the playing of an Earth/science/plant tag. The Engine is consistent here in a way that looks deliberate rather than accidental — Tags.count(tag, 'default') DOES add wild tags (Tags.ts:98-101), so a wild tag counts toward requirements and tag totals while not firing on-play triggers. Recorded because it is the kind of asymmetry a later reader would otherwise re-investigate.

entries.justification: Printed 47 M€ start with no tags, and the action 'Spend 4 M€ to increase (one of) your LOWEST production 1 step' — the implementation offers exactly the tied-lowest productions (the minimum scan seeds on megacredits production, which is the only production that can be negative, and rebuilds the tie list whenever a strictly lower value appears), charges 4 M€, and adds one step of the chosen production. canAct is player.canAfford(4), which is the right precondition: raising a lowest production is always possible, so affordability is the whole requirement.

entries.name: Valley Trust
entries.justification: Printed 37 M€ start, Earth tag, science discount, and the first action 'draw 3 Prelude cards, and play one of them. Discard the other two' — initialAction draws exactly 3 from the game's own prelude deck and hands them to PreludesExpansion.selectPreludeToPlay with remainders: 'discard', which plays the chosen one and discards the other two back to the prelude deck. The discount is declared as cardDiscount {tag: SCIENCE, amount: 2} with no 'per', which Card.getCardDiscount resolves as amount * tagCount, i.e. 4 M€ off a two-science-tag card — the same per-tag reading the Engine (and the printed game) applies to Point Luna's 'when you play an Earth tag, including this, draw a card'.

It is not that warnings are missing from the drawn preludes — selectPreludeToPlay does set the 'preludeFizzle' warning on any unplayable prelude (PreludesExpansion.ts:32-40) — it is that the corporation's initialAction has no channel to surface a warning on the initial-action option itself. ONE THING FOR ANOTHER PHASE, not a Valley Trust finding: choosing an unplayable prelude here routes into PreludesExpansion.fizzle, which discards it and grants 15 M€. That is shared Prelude-expansion machinery reached identically from the ordinary prelude phase (Player.ts:1462), so it belongs with whichever batch owns EccentricSponsor.ts:24 — I did not adjudicate whether the 15 M€ consolation is printed rules. cost/victoryPoints false because a corporation has neither; startingMegaCredits (37) and tags ([EARTH]) checked.

entries.name: Vitor
entries.justification: The printed corporation says 'You start with 45 M€'; the Engine sets startingMegaCredits to 48 with the comment 'It's 45 + 3 when this corp is played', i.e. it hard-codes Vitor triggering its own 'including this' effect even though Vitor carries no VP icon (its own onCardPlayed would return early on victoryPoints === undefined, so the +3 could never arise dynamically). Everything else matches: initialAction funds one not-yet-funded award for free via game.fundAward (no charge, and it does occupy one of the three award slots, correctly raising the cost of later awards), and onCardPlayed pays 3 M€ exactly for cards whose VP *icon* is non-negative, correctly excluding no-icon cards, negative fixed VP, and negative dynamic VP (it reads the icon value, not the currently-scored VP, which is the right reading of 'non-negative VP icon').
entries.printedText: Vitor (R35), Earth tag. 'You start with 45 M€. As your first action, fund an award for free.' Effect: 'When you play a card with a NON-NEGATIVE VP icon, including this, gain 3 M€.' I can state the 45 and the award clause with confidence; I cannot independently confirm the exact 'including this' wording, and that clause is the whole question — it is the only thing that could justify 48.
entries.notes: The open question is worth exactly 3 M€ of starting cash on 1 of 17 dealable corporations, so it is small but it is a resource divergence if the reading is wrong, and it is invisible to every other check in this audit. Internal evidence against: the card's own description string still says 'You start with 45 M€' and the renderer draws 45, so the UI shows 45 while the player receives 48 with no log entry explaining the difference. cost/victoryPoints marked false because a corporation card has neither field; startingMegaCredits (48) and tags ([EARTH], correct) were both checked. entries.name: Eccentric Sponsor

ranking.marker: src/server/cards/prelude/EccentricSponsor.ts:24 - TODO: prelude cannot detect during canPlay that it will fizzle (legality-relevant)

entries.justification: The printed mechanic is implemented exactly: a flat 25 M€ reduction on exactly one card played out of hand, keyed on `player.lastCardPlayed`, and — importantly — the discount is live while `PlayProjectCard` computes `getPlayableCards()`, so cards affordable only with the discount are correctly offered. What has no basis on the printed card is the failure path: when no card is playable the Engine grants +15 M€ and returns the prelude to the deck (`PreludesExpansion.fizzle`). Whether the printed Prelude rules compensate an unexecutable mandatory prelude at all, let alone with 15 M€, is a rules question I cannot settle; the only occurrences of the number in the repo are the Engine's own log string, UI warning and their translations, which is the same source, not evidence.
entries.printedText: Eccentric Sponsor (P11, prelude, no tags, no cost, no VP): 'Play a card from hand, reducing its cost by 25 M€.'
entries.notes: MARKER `EccentricSponsor.ts:24` characterised. The card overrides neither `canPlay` nor `bespokeCanPlay` and carries no `requirements` and no `behavior`, so `Card.canPlay` (Card.ts:242-260) is unconditionally true — that is exactly why the TODO exists, and it is the whole of the Ecology Experts asymmetry R1 flagged. The two cards take different code paths to the same rule: Ecology Experts' `canPlay` override returns false and `selectPreludeToPlay` fizzles it AT THE GATE, never calling `playCard`; Eccentric Sponsor is genuinely played, and fizzles from inside its own `bespokePlay` continuation after `PlayProjectCard` yields `undefined`. For Eccentric Sponsor the two paths converge on the identical outcome (+15 M€) because the card has no other on-play effect, no tags and no VP, so nothing is lost by being un-played; for Ecology Experts they do not converge (its +1 plant production is forfeited on the gate path). NO LEGALITY DIFFERENCE for Nadia: both preludes remain selectable in `selectPreludeToPlay` either way, so the enumerator's legal set is unaffected; the missing `preludeFizzle` warning is a client-side hint Nadia does not read. NO EXPLOIT: `PlayProjectCard` returns `undefined` only when `getPlayableCards()` is empty (PlayProjectCard.ts:13-17) — `SelectProjectCardToPlay` offers no decline option, so a player who CAN play a card cannot elect the 15 M€ instead. `EccentricSponsor.ts:39-40` clears `lastCardPlayed` on fizzle so the 25 M€ never leaks to a later card; belt-and-braces, since the fizzle also removes the card from the tableau. If W adjudicates the fizzle rule as unprinted, this card becomes a `behavioural-divergence` with magnitude exactly 15 M€ per fizzle, and the same ruling must be applied to Ecology Experts, Merger and Double Down (the other `fizzle` callers; only the first two are in scope).

entries.name: Ecology Experts
entries.justification: The printed prelude states two things unconditionally: increase your plant production 1 step, and play a card from hand ignoring global requirements. The Engine's canPlay override (lines 36-52) makes the whole prelude conditional on the second half being performable: it temporarily grants itself +50 to every global-parameter requirement and +1 plant production, then requires `player.getPlayableCards().length > 0`. When that is false - most obviously when the player bought no project cards at all during SelectInitialCards, or cannot afford any card in hand - PreludesExpansion.selectPreludeToPlay fizzles the prelude: +15 M€, card discarded, and the printed +1 plant production never happens. Whether an unperformable *benefit* on a prelude blocks the prelude is exactly the unsettled question the plan flagged; the Engine answers it inconsistently, refusing here but allowing Eccentric Sponsor to be played and fizzle afterwards. The probe itself is otherwise correct: the +1 plant production is included before testing playability (so a card gated on plant production is correctly considered), and the bonus is scoped to global parameters only, matching 'ignoring global requirements' rather than 'ignoring all requirements' (tests/cards/prelude/EcologyExperts.spec.ts confirms AI Central's science-tag requirement is not waived).
entries.printedText: Ecology Experts (P10), prelude, Plant + Microbe tags. 'Increase your plant production 1 step. PLAY A CARD FROM HAND, IGNORING GLOBAL REQUIREMENTS.'
entries.notes: Reachability is NOT low, unlike most findings in this batch: an empty starting hand is a perfectly ordinary outcome for a random-legal agent, and Ecology Experts was played 229 times in the 1,500-game sweep, so the fizzle path is very likely exercised. If W resolves this against the Engine the divergence is a resource swap (+15 M€ and a discarded prelude, instead of +1 plant production and a free card play) and escalates under K5. Two side-effects of the probe worth recording even if the verdict lands on `matches`: (a) canPlay mutates player state (temporaryGlobalParameterRequirementBonus, production.plants, and plants under Manutech) and restores it in a `finally`, so any snapshot taken mid-probe would be wrong - relevant to agent/src/engine/snapshot.ts if M4 search ever forks inside a canPlay; (b) getPlayableCards() calls canPlay on every card in hand, which can set transient `warnings` on those cards (e.g. Asteroid Mining Consortium's selfTarget).

merge.method: Batches R2-R6 ran concurrently and each wrote its own file, per the plan's ownership table (a shared file with concurrent writers is a lost-findings bug). Merged here with three checks: every queued card claimed by exactly one batch, no batch writing outside its own list, and no queued card left at `not-reviewed`.

crossBatch.title: Retroactive tag crediting for a card played from inside a prelude - three batches, three different verdicts on one mechanism
crossBatch.statement: When Ecology Experts defers a PlayProjectCard, the card that enters play afterwards is credited with Ecology Experts' own already-played tags. EcologicalZone.ts:66-76 implements this explicitly (a third animal); Decomposers.ts:48-53 does the same (+2 microbes, 3 where the printed card gives 1); Viral Enhancers has no such hack, although Ecology Experts carries both a plant and a microbe tag and Viral Enhancers responds to both. So the Engine cannot be right both ways: if the crediting is correct, Viral Enhancers under-fires by 2; if it is incorrect, Ecological Zone over-fires by 1 and Decomposers by 2.

verdicts.Ecological Zone: undecided (R1) - the Engine applies the rule consistently across the two cards that implement it, which is what a genuine "the nested play is simultaneous" reading would produce
verdicts.Decomposers: behavioural-divergence, escalating (R2) - the printed sequence is unambiguous: you place Ecology Experts and gain its tags before its text tells you to play a card, so an ongoing "when you play" effect cannot see a play that preceded it
verdicts.Viral Enhancers: matches (R5) - and R5's own reading (ongoing effects apply only from when the card is in play) makes Viral Enhancers correct and the other two the outliers

crossBatch.forW: Adjudicate all four together and give Ecological Zone and Decomposers the same verdict. They are the same mechanism and they currently differ only because two independent batches read them. Scoring-relevant either way (1 VP per 2 animals, 1 VP per 3 microbes), so the resolution decides whether this escalates under K5.

crossBatch.title: Identical gain-first code in two cards, and the two defects compound
crossBatch.statement: PowerSupplyConsortium.ts:35-45 is byte-for-byte identical to EnergyTapping.ts:35-45, comment included. When no player has energy production, both defer the gain first, making the player their own only legal target for the "decrease any energy production" step and handing the gain straight back. R3 read Energy Tapping and R2 read Power Supply Consortium independently and reached the same verdict. R2 answered R3's open question: Power Supply Consortium's printed requirement is 2 POWER TAGS, not energy production, so the zero-target branch is reachable - and Energy Tapping landing in its own zero-target branch is one of the ways to reach it, so the two defects compound on a concrete generation-1 line.
crossBatch.forW: One register row and one upstream report covering both cards, not two. Note the shared weakest link both batches recorded: the anchor is the general "do as much as you can, ignore what you cannot" rule plus written order, not a card-specific FAQ line either batch could quote. If W rejects that anchor, both entries become `undecided`, not `matches`. Great Escarpment Consortium and Asteroid Mining Consortium carry the same code but their printed steel/titanium-production requirements make the branch unreachable.

crossBatch.title: PreludesExpansion.fizzle grants 15 M€ with no printed basis - systemic, not per-card
crossBatch.statement: When a prelude cannot be played, the Engine discards it and grants 15 M€. Three batches hit this from three directions and none of them could find a printed basis for the 15 M€ anywhere in Prelude. It is also the mechanism behind an Engine inconsistency: Ecology Experts is refused at the selection gate by its own `canPlay` and then fizzles, whereas Eccentric Sponsor (the pre-located marker, EccentricSponsor.ts:24) is genuinely played and fizzles from inside `bespokePlay`. R2 established that for Eccentric Sponsor the two paths converge - it has no other on-play effect, no tags and no VP - so there is no legality difference for Nadia and no exploit. Valley Trust's initial action reaches the same shared machinery (Player.ts:1462).
crossBatch.forW: Adjudicate once as one systemic register entry rather than as seven card entries. The four paid preludes' own canAfford checks were each verified correct; they appear here only because the fizzle rule governs them. Reachable: Ecoline (36 M€) buying 10 initial cards leaves 6 M€.

crossBatch.title: "Remove up to N" is implemented as all-or-nothing across the whole attack class
crossBatch.statement: Both cards print "up to" and both offer only {maximum, none}, where the printed text grants any amount 0..N. R3 marked both non-escalating because it is a universal Engine convention for the whole attack class and the omitted amounts are dominated - with one non-contrived exception at 3-4p, where the Miner award counts steel plus titanium, so removing more from one opponent can hand the award to another. Flooding is the printed-text contrast that shows the distinction is real rather than a blanket excuse: it says "remove 4 M€" with no "up to", the implementation removes exactly 4, and it verdicts `matches`.
crossBatch.forW: Adjudicate once for the class. Names AC-5 (3-4p placement) as where it could first bite.

crossBatch.title: Actions whose entire printed effect raises an already-maxed global parameter are legal moves that do nothing
crossBatch.statement: The Engine's answer is yes-with-a-warning: canAct calls addWarning('maxoceans'/'maxtemp') and returns true, so paying 18 M€ for a 10th ocean or 8 heat at +8 C is an enabled, server-validated legal move with no effect. Deliberate and internally consistent (ArtificialLake.ts:35 says so outright), and the Engine is scrupulous about the TR half - increaseTemperature, increaseOxygenLevel and addOcean all return before granting TR. R4 could not settle it from printed card text, so all five are `undecided`.
crossBatch.forW: One register row, not five. Practical impact is confined to random-legal baselines burning resources; no evaluating agent picks a strictly dominated move, so M3+ is unaffected and no state is mis-scored either way.

crossBatch.title: Sell Patents' 0 plays in the sweep is an instrument blind spot, not a defect signal - a K4 correction, not a K5 finding
crossBatch.statement: Player.getActions() (Player.ts:1660-1664) calls the standard project's action() directly, and that path calls projectPlayed itself - it never reaches payAndExecute, which is the chokepoint agent/src/coverage/playSweep.ts wraps. Sell Patents is therefore structurally invisible to the sweep and would read 0 plays however often it was used.
crossBatch.forW: This corrects an entry in phase M's artifact, not phase R's. The `reachable-by-other-route` row cannot be discharged by card_play_coverage.json; the honest statement is "not observable by this instrument". Belongs to question 2/4, not question 3.

crossBatch.title: A mid-play snapshot can carry a negative resource count
crossBatch.statement: Moss.ts:33-42 and NitrophilicMoss.ts:34-42 accept the play when plants are short but Viral Enhancers is in the tableau, then bespokePlay does a raw `player.plants--`. That setter (Player.ts:225-227) assigns straight to stock, bypassing Stock.add's clamp AND its logIllegalState call (Stock.ts:24-41), so stock.plants transiently reaches -1 before onCardPlayed hands the plant back. It settles at 0, so no printed outcome differs and all three cards verdict correctly - Viral Enhancers grants exactly what its printed card promises.
crossBatch.forW: Not a rules finding. It is an Agent-side note for agent/src/engine/snapshot.ts and M4 search: a snapshot taken mid-play would capture a negative resource, and the Engine's own illegal-state logging is bypassed on exactly this path so nothing would flag it. Running Notes material.
